response.internal_assessment: Optimizing L1 STABILIZE — the savings drawdown is the central threat. I have $28,449 left and I am burning roughly $2,780 per month net. That is ten months of runway on paper, but it does not feel like ten months when you have two kids and a mortgage and a sector index that has been below 80 for months. The RoboRide chapter is closed. The Carlos Ruiz B2B channel is alive and just produced a real PO. Angela has my job description. Mark gave me two names. The storefront signage is up. The infrastructure is in place. This tick I need to do three things: accept Frank Russo's workshop offer and convert it into a visible signal to my B2B clients that my team knows EV diagnostics; push Carlos Ruiz from a one-off PO to a recurring monthly supply arrangement; and make a first direct call to Sarah Kim who has been in my relationship list since the beginning but has never had a dedicated customer discovery conversation. The Frank Russo workshop costs $400-600. That is real money at my burn rate. But if I walk Carlos and Sarah through the door of a store whose counter staff can talk EV diagnostics, that changes the sales conversation permanently. The cost is one-fifth of a Carlos order. I take it.

chosen_actions.description: Accept Frank Russo's offer to deliver a two-hour AV literacy and EV diagnostics workshop for Howard's Parts staff. Confirm date, content scope, and fee of $500 (midpoint). Ask Frank to include a brief segment on brake wear patterns in EV and hybrid vehicles specifically — this directly maps to what Carlos ordered and what Sarah's shop will need. Howard will invite Carlos Ruiz and Sarah Kim to attend as guests, framing it as a professional development session open to the mechanics in his B2B network. This converts a training cost into a relationship event.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: $500 workshop fee; two hours of staff time; goodwill with Carlos Ruiz and Sarah Kim if they attend
chosen_actions.reasoning: My skill_relevance score is 0.3. That is dangerous. The B2B pivot only works if my store is seen as technically credible by mechanics doing EV work. Frank Russo offering this workshop is a gift. The incremental cost against the relationship and credibility upside is asymmetric in my favor. Loss aversion says do not spend $500 when savings are falling. Agency and forward orientation say this $500 defends the entire B2B revenue strategy. I take the forward-looking position.

chosen_actions.description: Call Carlos Ruiz this week and propose converting the one-off PO relationship into a recurring monthly supply arrangement. Howard proposes a simple standing order: Carlos specifies his anticipated monthly consumption of brake hardware, hybrid diagnostic connectors, and safety consumables at the start of each month; Howard fulfills within 24 hours at a 5% loyalty discount off catalog price. No contract, no minimums — a handshake monthly commitment that Carlos can adjust or pause. The goal is to replace sporadic one-off orders with predictable monthly revenue. Howard asks Carlos directly: 'The $650 order last week — if that becomes a standing monthly order with a five percent discount built in, does that work for your shop?'
chosen_actions.resources_involved: 5% discount on recurring orders in exchange for monthly revenue predictability; Howard's inventory planning capacity
chosen_actions.reasoning: Carlos just demonstrated he is a real buyer — same-day response to my reallocation call, $650 PO for exactly the inventory I had. That is a customer who wants to buy from me. The shift from transactional to recurring is the revenue stabilization move I need. Even a $600/month standing order from Carlos, combined with similar arrangements from two or three other mechanics, starts to meaningfully offset the burn. This is the highest-leverage revenue action available this tick.

chosen_actions.description: Make a first dedicated call to Sarah Kim — not a check-in, a customer discovery conversation with the same structure I used for Carlos at tick 2. Howard asks: what EV and hybrid work is the shop taking on, what parts are hardest to source, what does the supply chain look like from her current distributors, and what would make Howard's Parts the obvious local first call. Howard also mentions the Frank Russo workshop and invites her to attend as a guest. This is intelligence-gathering and relationship investment simultaneously.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: One phone call; Frank Russo workshop invitation; no financial cost
chosen_actions.reasoning: Sarah Kim has been in my relationship file since the beginning with trust at 0.52. I have never had a direct customer discovery conversation with her. Carlos responded immediately when I treated him as a B2B partner rather than a walk-in customer. Sarah is likely the same. The cost of this call is zero. The upside is a second recurring supply relationship with a mechanic who is actively transitioning to EV work. I should have done this at tick 2.

response.inner_monologue: The RoboRide distraction cost me four months and some real money, but I closed it clean, Carlos is buying, and now I have a mechanic asking to teach my staff EV diagnostics — if I can turn this workshop into a client event instead of a cost, I might actually be building something here.
